item.title: Computational Investigation and Defect-Related Optimization of Lead-Free Cs₂AgBiBr₆ Double-Perovskite Solar Cells Using DFT, SCAPS-1D, and Machine Learning
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Sameer Pandey¹
The lead-free double perovskite materials have become attractive alternatives to the traditional lead-based photovoltaic (PV) absorbers in view of their relatively low toxicity to the environment. The electronic complexities and simulated PV performances of the lead-free double perovskite Cs₂AgBiBr₆ were investigated using complementary computational tools such as Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, device simulation through the SCAPS-1D code, and Machine Learning (ML). In the electronic structure calculations, we have used the quantum ESPRESSO package, with the generalized gradient approximation (GGA-PBE) functional. item.title: Explainable Point-Cloud Deep Learning for 3D Conformation Recognition of Temperature-Sensitive Bottlebrush Polymers
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Amirul Islam Saimon, Soumil Joshi, Jihoon Chung, Blake Johnson, Sanket Deshmukh, Zhenyu Kong
Bottlebrush polymers (BBPs) exhibit highly tunable physicochemical properties arising from their unique 3D architectures of densely grafted side chains. Accurately recognizing and classifying their conformations is critical for understanding structure-property relationships, yet remains challenging due to the complex geometries. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can generate 3D BBP conformations as bead-level coordinates that provide point cloud data for quantitative shape analysis. Conventional approaches either compress these data into hand-crafted geometric descriptors or discretize the structures onto 3D grids (voxelization) before applying data-driven models. item.title: RLVR landscapes for iterated multiplications can be benign: Insights from spin-glass theory

📚 arXiv
👤 Noa Rubin, Zohar Ringel
arXiv:2609.28625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the importance of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), the extent to which it can learn new reasoning capabilities remains debated. Here we study the optimization landscape of RLVR on algorithmic tasks, such as iterated group and quasigroup multiplication. To this end, we map entropy-regularized RLVR over myopic tabular policies onto an energy-based (spin-glass) model over deterministic policies. This mapping upper-bounds what RLVR can achieve, and lets us rigorously characterize the landscape in this tabular setting. We show, both theoretically and experimentally, that for a wide class of models and tasks with uncorrelated inputs, this landscape is benign, containing no local minima that could trap RLVR training.…
